land.text: the Đại Ngu lands of the Hồ, held by the Ming as Jiaozhi from 1407 and recovered by Lê Lợi

predecessors.note: The Ngô row ends in 1406 and its dossier hands the land to the Ming; Cliopatria's Ming shape holds it to 1428 and the Lê row begins in 1429.

land.text: Đàng Ngoài, the Lê court's north under the Trịnh lords

successors.note: Cliopatria's Lê row ends in 1571 and its Trịnh row begins in 1572 on the same land; the Trịnh page has the family at the head of the Lê court from 1545 and the Lê emperors 'rulers in name only', and the Lê dynasty itself runs to 1789.

land.text: Đàng Trong, the Lê south under the Nguyễn lords

successors.note: The Trịnh page has Nguyễn Hoàng 'increasingly secure in his rule over the southern province' and breaking relations with the court in 1600.

capitals.name: Đông Kinh (Thăng Long, Hanoi)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Đông Kinh (1428-1527 and 1592-1789)'; the Mạc then held it until 1592 (Mạc page).

capitals.name: Tây Đô (Tây Kinh, Thanh Hóa)
capitals.note: The Mạc page has Lê Trang Tông crowned in 1533 'at the recaptured Tây Đô castle'; the Trịnh page puts Tây Đô in Thanh Hóa as the temporary capital; the Lê infobox gives 'Tây Kinh (temp) (1543-1592)'. Coordinates approximate (the Hồ citadel).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1428: Cliopatria's Lê row begins in 1429 but 'Coronation of Lê Lợi: 29 April 1428' and 'the Ming dynasty withdrew by 1428'. The outline is the Đại Ngu land that the Ngô row ends with (453 cells, the 1429 shape without its Champa cells).

correction.text: Lê Lợi's Đại Việt at its enthronement: 'The dynasty officially began in 1428 with the enthronement of Lê Lợi'

keyframe_review.note: 151,670 km2 (510 cells). The Lê pages give no area (the Lê infobox has 7,700,000 people in 1490), so no ratio. 57 of the 510 cells (lat 14.6-16.1: Đà Nẵng and northern Quảng Nam) are Champa's until 1471: 'the border between Đại Việt and Champa was moved from Hải Vân Pass to Cù Mông Pass from 1471 till 1611'. The Champa dossier reaches the same verdict for its 1429 shape. Corrected to the 453-cell Đại Ngu core for 1429-1470.

correction.text: Đại Việt north of the Hải Vân Pass (applies 1429-1470 only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1471-1474: Cliopatria draws the annexation in 1475. 'On March 22, the city fell' (Vijaya, 1471) and 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên) was annexed to Đại Việt'; Thánh Tông 'established Quảng Nam as Đại Việt's 13th province'. Cliopatria's 1475 outline also takes Phú Yên and the edge of Khánh Hòa, which the page leaves to the Cham rump ('a ruler south of Bình Định (Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa) submitted as a vassal', undated), so they come off.

correction.text: Đại Việt with the annexed north of Champa, to the Cù Mông Pass (Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa stay Cham)

keyframe_review.note: 190,463 km2 (646 cells): the 1429 outline plus 136 Champa cells (the north of Champa, Phú Yên and the Central Highlands edge). The 1471 annexation and the Cù Mông border are the page's; Phú Yên (19 cells) and Khánh Hòa (2) come off, as the Champa dossier keeps them Cham to 1611. The Central Highlands cells (about 40) stay as the claim over the highland ruler who 'submitted to Thánh Tông as a vassal' (undated). The shape holds to 1526: Mạc Đăng Dung took the throne in 1527.

New keyframe 1533: the Lê restoration. 'The Revival Lê took all provinces south of the Red River' over c. 1530-1533 and Lê Trang Tông was crowned in 1533 at the recaptured Tây Đô castle (the Lê page: 'when the Lê dynasty was restored in 1533, the Mạc fled to the far north'). Cliopatria has Đại Việt (Mạc) hold the whole realm in 1529-1533.

correction.text: the Revival Lê in 1533, the provinces south of the Red River

keyframe_review.note: 103,645 km2 (341 cells), the Lê south of lat 20.0 with the Mạc holding the rest. The Mạc page has the Lê take 'all provinces south of the Red River' by 1533 and the Ming rule only in 1540 that 'the Mạc would govern the north and the Lê the south, below the Red River'; Cliopatria adds the 107 cells (northern Thanh Hóa, Ninh Bình, Nam Định, Hà Nam, the delta's south bank) only in 1540, so the 1540 outline is used for 1534-1539.

135,369 km2 (447 cells): the south of the Red River after the Ming ruling of 1540 ('Under Ming pressure, the Mạc submitted'; the Ming demoted the Lê to a dutongshisi). Phú Yên (19 cells) and part of Khánh Hòa (4) come off as Cham. The Mạc lost territory to the Trịnh from 1541 and the capital Thăng Long fell to the Trịnh in 1572 and was retaken in 1573, but the pages date no border change 1540-1563.

135,369 km2: the same outline. The Trịnh page has the Trịnh at the head of the Lê court from 1545 ('rulers in name only') and Nguyễn Hoàng 'increasingly secure in his rule over the southern province'; Cliopatria splits this outline into its Trịnh (150 cells) and Nguyễn (296 cells) rows in 1572. Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa come off as in 1540.

ledger.note: 29 April 1428: Lê Lợi is enthroned and founds the Lê dynasty. 'Coronation of Lê Lợi: 29 April 1428' after the Lam Sơn uprising of 1418-1427 ('By early 1427, Lê Lợi's forces had controlled most of northern Vietnam'; 'the Ming dynasty withdrew by 1428').

region.text: Đại Việt recovered from the Ming

ledger.note: 28 November 1470: Lê Thánh Tông sails against Champa. 'On November 28, 1470, a 100,000-strong Vietnamese naval expedition led by Thánh Tông himself set out from Hóa Châu'; fighting began on 24 February 1471.

region.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

ledger.note: 22 March 1471: Vijaya falls. 'Vijaya surrounded on March 19... On March 22, the city fell after a four-day siege' (Thị Nại citadel 18 March, Mễ Cần citadel in Quảng Ngãi 26 February).

region.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

ledger.note: 1471: Đại Việt annexes northern Champa. 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên) was annexed to Đại Việt'; Thánh Tông 'established Quảng Nam as Đại Việt's 13th province', with the border moved 'from Hải Vân Pass to Cù Mông Pass from 1471 till 1611'. Cliopatria draws this in 1475.

region.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

ledger.note: Fall 1479: Lê Thánh Tông invades Lan Xang. 'In fall 1479, Thánh Tông led an army of 180,000 men marched westward, attacked Muang Phuan, Lan Xang and Nan'; 'Luang Phabang was captured and the Laotian ruler Chakkaphat was killed'. Mirrors lan-xang's contest_start of 1479. [reviewer se-01-f]

region.text: Luang Phabang, the Lan Xang capital, and its province

ledger.note: November 1484: 'By November 1484, Thanh Tong and his forces had withdrawn back to Dai Viet'; no land was kept. Mirrors lan-xang's contest_end of 1484. [reviewer se-01-f]

region.text: Luang Phabang, the Lan Xang capital, and its province

ledger.note: 15 June 1527: Mạc Đăng Dung usurps the throne. 'Mạc Đăng Dung usurped the throne: 15 June 1527'; the Mạc page: 'In 1527 Mạc Đăng Dung removed Lê Cung Hoàng and proclaimed himself as Emperor'. The Mạc hold the realm; Cliopatria's Đại Việt row begins in 1529.

region.text: the whole realm as corrected for 1475-1526 (without Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa, Cham to 1611), to the Mạc

ledger.note: 1533: the Revival Lê holds the provinces south of the Red River. 'The Revival Lê took all provinces south of the Red River' over c. 1530-1533 (the page's span; the region is its words) and Lê Trang Tông was crowned in 1533 at the recaptured Tây Đô castle; the Ming confirmed the division in 1540.

region.text: the Lê lands 'south of the Red River' under the Ming ruling of 1540, to the Cù Mông Pass

ledger.note: 1571: the Nguyễn south is drawn as a separate state. Page silent on 1571-1572: the Trịnh page has Nguyễn Hoàng ruling the southern province and breaking relations with the Trịnh-dominated court in 1600; Cliopatria's Nguyễn lords row begins in 1572 with the 296 cells of Lê's south.

1571: the Lê land passes to the Trịnh and Nguyễn lords in Cliopatria's rows. Page silent on 1571; the Trịnh page: 'Established: 1545' (Trịnh Kiểm at the head of the Lê court), the Lê emperors 'rulers in name only'; the Lê dynasty itself continues to 1789 and the Lê page's infobox ends the Revival Lê in 1789. Colour continues with the Trịnh lords.

region.text: the Lê lands, to the Trịnh lords (north) and Nguyễn lords (south)

wars.name: Lam Sơn uprising
wars.outcome: Lê Lợi's rebellion ('began on the day after Tết in February 1418'; Battle of Tốt Động-Chúc Động in October 1426) drove out the Ming, who withdrew by 1428; Lê Lợi was crowned on 29 April 1428.
wars.note: The contest and rebel-held phase 1418-1427 predates the Lê dossier's life; the Ming dossier should carry it with counterpart le-dynasty.

wars.name: Champa-Đại Việt War (1471)

zones.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

wars.outcome: Vijaya fell on 22 March 1471; northern Champa was annexed and the border moved to the Cù Mông Pass; the Cham court survived at Panduranga and two Cham rulers submitted as vassals.
wars.note: A guerrilla revolt of 1474 under Bố Trì Trì and Trà Toại was suppressed (page).

wars.name: Lê invasion of Lan Xang

zones.text: Luang Phabang, the Lan Xang capital, and its province

wars.outcome: 'In fall 1479, Thánh Tông led an army of 180,000 men' and 'Luang Phabang was captured and the Laotian ruler Chakkaphat was killed'; no Lê territory was added (the Lan Xang dossier carries the contest over Luang Prabang, 1479-1484).
wars.note: The same page has Thánh Tông make Muang Phuan a prefecture of Đại Việt in 1471; Muang Phuan lies outside Cliopatria's Lê outline and no page opened gives its end, so it is not drawn.

wars.name: Lê-Mạc War

zones.text: northern Thanh Hóa and the Red River delta's south bank, held by the Lê from 1533 and confirmed by the Ming in 1540

wars.outcome: The Revival Lê took the provinces south of the Red River; the Ming ruled in 1540 that the Mạc governed the north and the Lê the south; the Mạc lost territory to the Trịnh from 1541, Thăng Long fell in 1572 and was retaken in 1573, and in 1592 Trịnh Tùng conquered Hanoi and the northern provinces; the Mạc retreated to Cao Bằng.
wars.note: The page gives no formal 1533-1592 range for the war; after 1571 the war is the Trịnh lords' dossier.

certainty.note: The Ming frontier in the north is approximate; no treaty line is dated on the pages.

The Cù Mông Pass border with Champa (1471-1611) is a named pass but the page gives no treaty or survey; the Central Highlands and Lan Xang edges are claims; the Red River line of 1540 is the Ming's ruling.

notes: Cliopatria's Lê row has three problems the pages settle: the 1429-1474 shape includes 57 Champa cells (the Hải Vân-Cù Mông border moved only in 1471, so the Champa dossier also marks its 1429 shape wrong); the 1475 shape includes Phú Yên and the edge of Khánh Hòa, which stay Cham to 1611; and the 1534-1539 outline is the 1540 one on the Mạc page's wording ('all provinces south of the Red River' by 1533). The Lê pages give no area, so there is no infobox ratio. State boundaries: this dossier runs 1428-1571 because Cliopatria splits the Lê court's land into 'Trịnh lords' and 'Nguyễn lords' rows from 1572. The Lê dynasty page runs the dynasty to 1789 and the Trịnh page has the Trịnh at the head of the court from 1545, so the end year is Cliopatria's (confidence 1); the Trịnh dossier is the Lê court's continuation. The Mạc (Cliopatria 'Đại Việt', slug ai-viet, 1529-1833) holds the realm 1527-1533 and the delta north of the Red River after; the Revival Lê's first years (1533-1542) are placed at Tây Đô on the Mạc and Trịnh pages, while the Lê page's infobox gives Tây Kinh 1543-1592. Not drawn: Muang Phuan (a prefecture from 1471, outside the outline); the Central Highlands vassal and the coastal vassal rulers of 1471 (undated); the Ming frontier in the north (Guangxi and Yunnan edges, nothing dated on the pages opened); the Lam Sơn rebel phase of 1418-1427 (the Ming dossier should carry it). No ruler list was opened (Lê Lợi 1428-1433, Thái Tông 1433-1442, Thánh Tông 1460-1497 are on the pages, but the Nhân Tông and later reigns are not). Counterparts: ming-dynasty (ea-07), champa, ai-viet, trinh-lords, nguyen-lords, lan-xang (all slugs of se-01 except the Ming).
